in_ClaimDataJSON.description: Claim details extracted on previous steps

in_AssessmentReportJSON.description: Validated assessor report converted to structured JSON.

in_EligibilityDecision.description: The human reviewer's decision at the eligibility gateway. An approval makes every finding in in_EligibilityChecksJSON a granted exception, not an open breach.

in_EligibilityNotes.description: The reviewer's own note explaining that decision. Where it contradicts a finding, the note wins.

in_PreviousClaimsJSON.description: Claims already settled against this policy in the current policy period, as a JSON document. An empty priorClaims array means none, which is an answer rather than missing data.

out_PayoutChecksJSON.description: Results of payout analysis  Check envelope — see contracts/check-envelope.md. Every string is shown to a human reviewer.

verdict.description: pass when nothing needs a human; attention when a reviewer should look; fail when this analysis blocks the claim.

headline.description: One line the reviewer can act on. States the reason, not the outcome.

summary.description: Your reasoning. Replaces the separate summary output that used to exist.

checks.description: One entry per thing you checked, reported whether it passed or not.

label.description: Sentence case, written for a claims reviewer. Never a payload field name.

status.description: warn when satisfied only with a caveat, or when data needed for the check was unavailable.

verdict.description: The one-line result shown beside the label.

details.description: Supporting evidence for this check, up to 6 rows. Supply it for every check, passing ones included — a reviewer can expand a passing check to see what was compared.

out_SettlementJSON.description: The settlement table — see contracts/settlement-table.md. Every amount is a JSON number, never a formatted string; the currency is stated once. Declared but not required: a table that fails to arrive is reported by the app as a contract violation, whereas a missing required output faults the whole job.

currency.description: ISO code for every amount in this table, e.g. RON, EUR, HKD, INR. Stated once; never repeated per row.

recommended.description: What this agent calculates. Never edited by anyone downstream — an assessor's changes become a separate 'final' block written by the app.

rows.description: One row per damage item on the claim, in the claim's order. Every item gets a row, covered or not. Omit Coverage D rows when no additional living expenses were claimed.

section.description: Your judgement, not a lookup from the claim's category text. A garage, shed, fence, gate or pathway is B even when its category reads 'Structure - …'.

label.description: Short human-facing name for the item, from the claim. Never a payload field name.

detail.description: The item as the claimant described it.

claimed.description: The claimed amount with all formatting stripped: 28000, never '28,000.00 lei'.

assessorEstimate.description: The assessor's figure for this same item, matched on meaning rather than position. Omit when the assessor did not price it, and say so in item_valuation.

cap.description: The limit that actually binds this row.

capSource.description: Which limit 'cap' is: the section limit, a Coverage C special sublimit, or what earlier claims have left.

exclusionReason.description: Required when covered is false. Never express an exclusion as a cap of 0 — a reader cannot tell that from an exhausted limit.

payable.description: This row's amount BEFORE the deductible. Never spread the deductible across rows.

subtotalABC.description: Sum of payable across Coverage A, B and C rows.

deductible.description: Applied once to subtotalABC, never to loss of use.

lossOfUse.description: Coverage D total, 0 when nothing was claimed.

net.description: subtotalABC - deductible + lossOfUse, never negative. If the deductible exceeds subtotalABC those coverages pay nothing and net is lossOfUse alone — a valid covered claim paying zero, not a denial.
